extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders (e.g., school bus operators, industry groups, safety advocates) who may submit comments on FMCSA docket FMCSA-2022-0148
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural/legal guidance for submitting public comments on the National School Transportation Association's application to renew an exemption from the CDL 'under-the-hood' pre-trip inspection requirement, and the agency's standards for evaluating that exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before July 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments received before the close of business on the comment closing date will be considered and available for examination in the docket; comments received after the date will be filed in the public docket and considered to the extent practicable. FMCSA will continue to file, in the public docket, relevant information that becomes available after the comment closing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted submission methods and single-method rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments using the Federal eRulemaking Portal (www.regulations.gov), by mail, hand delivery/courier, or fax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only one of these means for your submission. For online submission, put the docket number 'FMCSA-2022-0148' in the 'Keyword' box, click 'Comment', type your comment, choose whether submitting as an individual or on behalf of a third party, and then submit. Fax is (202) 493-2251. Mail to Docket Operations, U.S. DOT, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, West Building, Ground Floor, Washington, DC 20590-0001. Hand deliveries accepted at the same address between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET, Monday–Friday (call ahead to confirm assistance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required docket identification on each submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission must include the Agency name and the docket number for this notice (FMCSA-2022-0148).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the docket number ensures your comment is posted to the correct public docket. For online submissions, enter the docket number in Regulations.gov search; for mailed/hand-delivered submissions, include the docket number on the submission itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content guidance for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a comment, indicate the specific section of this document to which the comment applies and provide a reason for your suggestions or recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMCSA recommends including your name and a mailing address, email address, or phone number in the body of your document so the Agency can contact you if it has questions. State whether you are submitting as an individual or on behalf of a third party. Comments should explain the rationale (e.g., safety concerns, data, operational impacts) supporting the position taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail/hand-delivery formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit comments by mail or hand delivery, submit them in an unbound format, no larger than 8 1/2 by 11 inches, suitable for copying and electronic filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit comments by mail and want confirmation they reached the facility, enclose a stamped, self-addressed postcard or envelope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner and relevant to the notice; CBI is exempt from public disclosure under FOIA (5 U.S.C. 552).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your comments contain CBI, clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI and mark each page that constitutes CBI as 'PROPIN'. Send CBI submissions to Brian Dahlin, Chief, Regulatory Evaluation Division, Office of Policy, FMCSA, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590-0001 or via email at brian.g.dahlin@dot.gov. FMCSA will treat such marked submissions as confidential and they will not be placed in the public docket. At this time, you need not send a duplicate hardcopy of electronic CBI submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and public posting of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT posts all comments received without change to www.regulations.gov, including any personal information included in a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are posted without edit and are searchable by the name of the submitter. Agencies may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions) and submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them. Be aware that information you include may become publicly searchable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket inspection and physical access
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not have internet access, you may view the docket by visiting Docket Operations on the ground floor of the DOT West Building, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., ET, Monday–Friday, except Federal holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be sure someone is there to help you, call (202) 366-9317 or (202) 366-9826 before visiting Docket Operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal basis and procedural requirements for exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA has authority under 49 U.S.C. 31136(e) and 31315(b) to grant exemptions from the FMCSRs and must publish a notice of each exemption request (49 CFR 381.315(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency must provide the public an opportunity to inspect information relevant to the application, including the applicant's safety analyses. The Agency reviews safety analyses and public comments and determines whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved by the current regulation (49 CFR 381.305(a)). The Agency must publish its decision in the Federal Register (49 CFR 381.315(b)) and, if granted, identify the regulatory provision(s) exempted, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)). If denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)). The exemption may be renewed (49 CFR 381.300(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive issues commenters should consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should address whether renewal of the exemption would be appropriate given safety and operational considerations, including whether the exemption achieves a level of safety equivalent to or greater than current regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant matters include the applicant's safety analyses, evidence regarding recruitment and workforce impacts, training resource allocation, operational impacts of removing the 'under-the-hood' testing requirement, any safety data indicating positive or negative impacts, and whether restrictions (e.g., intrastate-only operation) are appropriate. FMCSA will consider these materials when determining whether to renew the exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of existing/proposed exemption to reference in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The current exemption permits CDL applicants seeking a school bus endorsement to forgo the engine compartment portion of the pre-trip inspection skills test and restricts drivers issued CDLs pursuant to the exemption to intrastate operation of school buses only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may reference the effective period of the current exemption (Nov 28, 2022–Nov 28, 2024) and NSTA's request for a three-year renewal when arguing for or against renewal. FMCSA's previous analysis determined the original exemption was likely to achieve equivalent or greater safety; commenters may provide new or contrary evidence.
